subject: Ownership handling & feedback license: ClientCo redlines
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clientco.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@clientco.com, dan.reed@clientco.com
Date: 2026-06-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ClientCo redlines - MSA & Order Form (output + training)

Hi Karthik,

Attached are our legal team's redlines to your MSA and the proposed order form. Two items we need clarity on so we can proceed to procurement:

1) Output entitlement: The redline proposes that Customer "shall own" output but excludes proprietary Redwood system outputs. We'd like explicit confirmation that output generated from customer prompts and customer data will be assignable to us for downstream productization. We flagged your current language as ambiguous for some developer-generated outputs.

2) Training / feedback license: The redline removes an unrestricted feedback license and instead asks for an explicit opt-in. We understand Redwood's model improvement needs; request: either limit feedback use to aggregated telemetry (no raw content) or provide a clear process to request deletion/exclusion.

Can you route to legal and product? We've attached marked-up files: ClientCo_MSA_redline.docx and ClientCo_OrderForm_redline.pdf. We'd like to close this in the next week if possible.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Legal Operations
ClientCo

Attachments:
- ClientCo_MSA_redline.docx (docx)
- ClientCo_OrderForm_redline.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clientco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClientCo redlines - MSA & Order Form (output + training)

Maria — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. Routing to legal (Laura) and product/ops (Priyom) for quick review. Quick notes from my side before we do a formal redline:

- We are aligned in principle that customer-generated outputs should be usable by the customer; the ask is to make sure we preserve ability to improve models in ways that don't expose customer content.
- For feedback: Redwood typically requests a limited, nonexclusive, sublicensable feedback license for the purposes of improving models, subject to privacy constraints. We can discuss narrowed telemetry-only approaches for regulated customers.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura to provide law team's counter-language and a short rationale for any carveouts.
2) Priyom to outline product guardrails (aggregation, retention windows, opt-out mechanics).
3) Schedule a 30-min sync by EOD Thursday (I've copied calendar availability in a follow-up).

Attaching a short internal summary of the asks so folks can triage.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: internal_summary_karthik_20260623.md

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clientco.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-24T08:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClientCo redlines - MSA & Order Form (output + training)

Thanks for the context — I reviewed the redlines (ClientCo_MSA_redline.docx) and drafted recommended compromise language (see attached redline_suggestions_laura.docx). High-level positions:

1) Output ownership / assignment
Proposed compromise: Customer shall have ownership of "Customer Output" defined as results generated solely by Customer Data and Customer Prompts. Redwood reserves title to "System Content" (pretrained weights, proprietary prompts, internal tooling). We add a short definition and an examples list to reduce ambiguity (e.g., templates generated from Redwood prompts excluded).

Suggested insertion (short form):
"Customer Output" means content generated by the Services that is the direct result of Customer Data and Customer Prompts. Customer may use, reproduce, modify and distribute Customer Output subject to the agreed Service terms. Redwood retains ownership of underlying model weights, system prompts, and model improvements.

2) Feedback / training license
Options to present to ClientCo: a) Limited telemetry-only license: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for model improvement; raw Customer Data and Customer Output are never ingested for training without explicit opt-in; OR b) Scoped feedback license with opt-out: Redwood may use Customer Feedback for model improvements but Customer may instruct Redwood to exclude specific datasets via a process defined in the Order Form.

Given ClientCo's posture, I recommend we offer option (a) as the default and (b) as an add-on for customers who want opt-in only. Implementation notes below describe the retention window and deletion request process.

3) Evidence & controls
Laura suggests including an appendix (Order Form exhibit) that lists the operational controls: retention windows, data segregation, telemetry types, and contact for exclusion requests. This reduces procurement friction.

I'll be available for a call Tue/Thu; happy to present the language live.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_suggestions_laura.docx

From: Daniel Reed <dan.reed@clientco.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clientco.com>, contracts@clientco.com
Date: 2026-06-25T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClientCo redlines - MSA & Order Form (output + training)

Laura — thanks for the quick read. A few clarifications from procurement/legal at ClientCo:

- The example list in your suggested definition is helpful, but we want explicit language covering compound outputs (e.g., outputs that combine Customer Data with public model knowledge). We need assurance those are still Customer Output if they materially reflect customer input.
- On the feedback license, our finance and privacy teams prefer (b) scoped feedback license with a clear, enforceable opt-out process. Aggregated telemetry is acceptable for exploratory improvements but not for model retraining tied to our data unless we explicitly opt in.

If Redwood can provide an exhibit that shows the opt-out mechanics (API or support ticket flow), retention schedules, and a sample commitment on response times, we can take this back to procurement and legal for a fast sign-off.

Also, please confirm whether this solution applies to embeddings and persisted vector stores — our internal teams use embeddings heavily and are concerned about co-mingling.

Thanks — happy to discuss on a call.

Daniel Reed
Sr. Contracts Manager, ClientCo

Links: DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/ClientCo/DC-91234

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@clientco.com>, Daniel Reed <dan.reed@clientco.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-28T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClientCo redlines - MSA & Order Form (output + training)

Daniel / Maria — thanks, acknowledged. Proposed immediate next steps so we keep momentum:

1) We will present two paths in a short exhibit attached to the Order Form: 
   - Path A (Default): Aggregated, de-identified telemetry only; no raw customer data used for model retraining. Includes retention windows and telemetry examples.
   - Path B (Opt-in): Scoped feedback license for retraining; explicit opt-in via Order Form checkbox + documented exclusion process.

2) We'll include explicit language re: compound outputs that ties "Customer Output" ownership to material contribution from Customer Data/Prompts (legal will draft a concise test).

3) Priyom will produce a short operational appendix addressing embeddings/vector stores, segregation, and support flow for opt-out/delete requests.

Laura and I will prepare the exhibit and a one-pager for procurement by Tuesday EOD. Can you confirm 30 minutes on Wednesday at 10am PT for a legal/ops sync? Calendar invite attached.

Appreciate the speed here — we'll aim to make the procurement checklist explicit to avoid back-and-forth.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachment: calendar_invite_call.ics
